Any number you compute off it (₹43K ÷ 17 ≈ ₹2,529) will swing wildly if the next three days bring 4 conversions or 14. Let it run until you hit roughly 100 conversions, or a clean 2-3 week window, whichever comes first — that's the threshold where CAC stops jumping around and starts meaning something. Until then, the only correct move is to keep it live, keep the spend steady, and stop refreshing the dashboard. The decision isn't ready, and pretending it is costs you more than waiting.

B2B SaaS with API-level deals can also have a long consideration lag, so some of these 17 may still be maturing and more may land late — another reason not to read a verdict into day 5.

an0270.user: Need help, two dashboards are driving me insane. D2C eyewear, Google Search, last 30 days, post-iOS. Meta-style platform reporting says ROAS 4.5, but Shopify last-click says 1.8. We spent ₹13L. Same period, same spend, completely different story. Which one is actually real? What's wrong with my tracking?
an0270.assistant:
Nothing's "wrong" with your tracking — both dashboards are working as designed, and both are biased in opposite directions. That's why they'll never agree, and chasing which one is "real" is a game with no winner.

The platform's 4.5 is inflated: post-iOS it leans on modelled (estimated) conversions and a 7-day-click window, so it generously claims credit for sales it only assumes it influenced. Shopify last-click's 1.8 is the opposite — it hands 100% of the credit to whoever the buyer clicked last, which systematically under-credits the ad that first created the demand and over-credits brand/direct/email at the bottom. The truth sits somewhere between 1.8 and 4.5, and no amount of squinting at either dashboard pins it down.

So stop refereeing the two. Anchor on a number neither can spin: blended CAC. Take total spend across everything (₹13L for the period) and divide by actual new customers from Shopify — real humans who paid, counted once. Manage to that single figure month over month. If blended CAC sits comfortably under your contribution per customer, you're winning regardless of what either ROAS says.

Caveat: blended CAC is bluntest when one channel dominates spend — if Search is most of your budget, it's a clean proxy; if you're running several channels heavily, blended hides which one is actually pulling, and you'll eventually want a holdout/geo test to settle that. But as the day-to-day steering metric, it beats two dashboards that will argue forever.

an0274.user: How do I lower my CAC? New to this. D2C snacks, mostly organic/SEO. Last 30 days: AOV ₹1,100, gross margin 31%, CAC ₹451, ROAS 2.4, CTR 2%. I keep thinking if I can just get CAC down a bit everything will click into place. What's the fastest way to bring it down?

The problem is wearing a marketing costume but it's a margin problem underneath. You need margin north of ~41% just for these ads to break even at today's CAC, and a real cushion above that.

Caveat: I'm reading gross margin as your true landed cost (product + packaging + shipping + payment fees). If shipping and fees aren't already in that 31%, your real position is worse, not better — confirm what's inside that number before you decide which lever to pull.
